source.behavior: Validated marked page data latches hasPageDataResponse and uses setTimeout(finish, 0); generic response still schedules 80ms; same validator, 2s hard deadline, observer cleanup and final animation frame. Source diff also changes explanatory comments.

outlier.classification: Marked-page data completes after navigation push; changed fast branch cannot have run. Untraced post-push delay is consistent with an existing React commit deadline, but exact causal attribution for this run is inference.

requestAccounting.caveat: Zero harness failures does not mean no aborted streams. Existing ERR_ABORTED accounting treats some status200 RSC streams separately. Request capture ends 250ms after readiness; do not infer a reduction in total recovery/background requests.

limitations: Five samples per side/input/condition, overlapping ranges and substantial local spread; no established full-path speedup or equivalence.
The 518.8ms after default immediate outlier is retained, not discarded.
Default touch shows a lower median, but its exploratory exact median permutation p is about 0.119; default immediate p is about 0.381.

The 1042.5ms after constrained profile is diagnostic only, not a sixth untraced latency sample. Separate source/trace evidence identifies unchanged React throttled commit timing and later JS, not the modified marked-page branch.
Synthetic constrained desktop settings do not represent a physical mobile device or production network.
Trace CPU sample weights and wall intervals are approximate and not additive CPU budgets.

diagnostics.purpose: Source-matched branch proof from eight separate diagnostic profiles; not a before/after performance estimate.

constrainedCause.purpose: Explain constrained diagnostic trace variance; not a before/after performance estimate.

appGate.interpretation: Both profiles take generic tree fallback. Only delivered ResourceTiming entry is unmarked tree; marked-page branch never used. Three destination RSC requests on each side.

reactCommitTimers.interpretation: After has explicit React commit delay, including a239ms gate after initial route chunks finish. No corresponding timer occurs before artifact in before profile.

interpretation: Pre-push app gate unchanged; after push4.553ms earlier.
After initial page body and route chunk requests arrive later; last initial route script completes68.827ms later.
After post-script interval to SDK request expands from76.229ms to306.534ms. Source-matched React commit timer109 explicitly waits239ms within this interval.
Approval request duration changes only92.958ms to95.848ms. Its298.230ms later start follows delayed hydration and does not originate the pre-artifact delay.

Do not add overlapping throttle waits to derive a total speed regression: timer108 overlaps route script loading. Profiles are diagnostic, not population estimates.

remainingLimiters: Successful marked-page delivery still precedes navigation; ResourceTiming responseEnd and reader EOF do not prove Next cache readiness.
Initial route JavaScript delivery, evaluation, React render/commit, then approval-review HTTP remain on the click-to-review-ready path.
Constrained runs retain generic fallback and three destination RSC requests; prior partial-head fallback mechanism is unmodified.

After-constrained trace has an explicit239ms React commit throttle after initial route scripts, absent pre-artifact in before-constrained. The earlier289ms throttle overlaps downloads; never sum them.
caveats: Diagnostic times include hooks/profiling overhead; excluded from untraced before/after claims.
ResourceTiming responseEnd, readerEOF, observer delivery, and cache readiness are distinct.
CPU sampled weights and main-task wall intervals are not exact additive CPU time.
Chrome ResourceFinish timestamps are timeline observations; source initiator is kept for attribution.
CDP marks some status200 Next RSC streams net::ERR_ABORTED while body-probe reports reader EOF; use the unchanged harness aborted-stream classification for failures.
All application final-frame callbacks and deadline cleanup are observed. All six default profiles exercise marked branch; both constrained profiles finish through generic fallback.
No trace-derived end-to-end speedup/regression claim is justified; parent runs unchanged untraced harness for that comparison.

requestTimingUnits: Script/HTTP request startMs is relative to harness wallStart, not native click. Profile times and sessionOpen metrics are click-relative. Request capture ends 250ms after observed readiness; no total query-reduction claim.
